name: Linear Motor Platform Standardization
summary: A shared linear-motor architecture for the POSEIDON and ICARUS large-format additive-manufacturing platforms.

bullets.text: Replaced servo-driven ballscrew assemblies and demonstrated 4-micron precision with a 30 kg moving mass at 4 m/s.
Unified product architecture and created swappable mounts to reduce support complexity and make future scaling easier.

additionalInfo.title: Linear Motor Platform Standardization
additionalInfo.subtitle: Higher-speed precision through a shared motion architecture
additionalInfo.problem: POSEIDON and ICARUS used servo-driven ballscrew assemblies that limited the opportunity to standardize service, mounts, and future performance across the product line.
constraints: Move a 30 kg machine assembly
Support large-format printer geometries
Preserve precision at high travel speed
Keep mounts serviceable across products
approach: Converted both flagship platforms to linear-motor assemblies
Unified the architecture between products
Designed easily swappable mounts
Validated speed and positional performance on the machine platforms
impact: Achieved 4-micron precision at 4 m/s with a 30 kg moving mass
Reduced product-to-product architectural complexity
Created a more scalable foundation for support and future performance

name: Automated LabVIEW Metrology System
summary: An automated measurement utility that collects high-frequency laser-sensor data over Modbus and turns it into tolerance charts.

bullets.text: Collected nine data points every 100 ms from multiple sensors without manual transcription.
Generated charts that made dimensional tolerance results directly usable by the end customer.

additionalInfo.title: Automated LabVIEW Metrology
additionalInfo.subtitle: High-frequency sensor collection translated into tolerance insight
additionalInfo.problem: Multiple laser-sensor readings needed to be collected consistently and transformed into a visual tolerance result that an end customer could use.
constraints: Communicate with multiple sensors over Modbus
Collect nine data points every 100 ms
Remove manual data-collection steps
Present results as an understandable tolerance chart
approach: Built the acquisition workflow in LabVIEW
Connected and polled multiple laser sensors through Modbus
Structured the incoming readings for repeatable analysis
Generated charts showing the tolerance of the measured data
impact: Automated a previously manual measurement workflow
Delivered consistent high-frequency data collection
Made measurement tolerance visible to the end customer

Control a large custom gantry
Prevent uncontrolled Z-axis motion during power loss

Implemented industrial-servo XY motion
Integrated dual-extrusion capability into the custom gantry platform

Improved the system's production orientation and motion safety
